title: Adventure World Expansion Sprint
specification:
# Adventure World Expansion Sprint

This PRD is intentionally lane-pure. PM should decompose it into a large adventure-only sprint for `adventure-agent`.

## Product Goal

Turn adventure into a broader exploration-and-encounter experience with more interesting traversal beats, stronger creature / combat variety, clearer objective structure, and a better sense of world progression.

The player experience should move from a basic roam-and-fight loop toward:

- clearer goals
- richer encounters
- more meaningful capture / progression choices
- stronger world identity across a longer run

## Sprint Shape

Expected shape:

- 10 to 14 implementation tasks
- all tasks assigned to `adventure-agent`
- one shared adventure lane branch
- one adventure PR with many commits
- no cross-lane work

Each task should still be atomic enough for one commit.

## Scope Boundaries

Stay inside:

- `src/barebones-starter/games/apps/adventure/**`

Primary areas likely to matter:

- `config.ts`
- `world.ts`
- `step.ts`
- `draw.ts`
- `constants.ts`
- `types.ts`
- `state.ts`
- `actors/**`
- `logic/**` if introduced or already present

## Deliverable Themes

PM should cover most of these themes.

### 1. World Structure and Objective Flow

- introduce clearer objectives, checkpoints, contracts, or run goals
- improve pacing from early exploration to more dangerous encounters
- make world progression easier to understand moment to moment

### 2. Encounter and Combat Depth

- expand enemy or creature archetype diversity
- improve encounter composition and pressure scaling
- create more distinct combat decisions beyond simple repetition

### 3. Capture / Companion / Progression Layer

- deepen creature capture, recruitment, or progression systems
- make collected or captured creatures matter more to the player’s long-term choices
- improve clarity around why certain creatures are valuable

### 4. Traversal and Biome Identity

- strengthen zone variation or environmental identity
- improve transitions between safer and riskier spaces
- make the map feel more deliberate than a flat play space

### 5. UI and Run Feedback

- improve run-state readability
- make player status, encounter context, and progress messaging clearer
- add better feedback for major progression events

### 6. End-of-Run / Mid-Run Summary Signals

- give the player better closure or reflection on what changed during the run
- improve milestone, unlock, or objective messaging

## Planning Rules For PM

- Do not emit tasks for other agents.
- Do not emit reviewer tasks.
- Prefer real gameplay, world, combat, and progression work over placeholder notes.
- Prefer building on existing adventure structures over creating detached scaffolding.
- Make the task list broad enough that the resulting PR becomes a real multi-commit sprint.
- Include tests only where they fit naturally into existing patterns.

## Definition Of Done

- Adventure feels materially larger and more directed.
- The sprint deepens exploration, encounters, and progression together.
- The work spans multiple adventure subsystems.
- The final lane PR should plausibly contain many commits because the task plan is large and real.

## Explicit Non-Goals

- no changes outside adventure scope
- no filler tasks created only to inflate commit count
- no PM-generated reviewer work
requirements: Produce between 10 and 14 implementation tasks total.
Assign every implementation task to adventure-agent only.
Do not create tasks for aquarium-agent
Keep every task scoped to files under src/barebones-starter/games/apps/adventure/ only.
Tasks must be atomic enough to land as one commit each on the shared adventure lane branch.
The resulting implementation should feel like one large adventure sprint rather than isolated note files.
The reviewer should merge one adventure PR after the lane finishes all tasks.

tasks.title: Add biome map foundations and zone metadata
tasks.description: Expand the flat adventure map into named biomes with explicit zone metadata, danger tiers, and visual identity so later progression and encounter systems can key off a structured world.
acceptance: `AdventureTile` or equivalent zone data supports more than the current single-grass overworld and `createAdventureState()` seeds at least four named regions.
Adventure world data includes per-zone ids, names, and danger tiers that other systems can reference.
World rendering clearly differentiates biome transitions during play through colors, overlays, or tile treatment.

tasks.title: Add route checkpoints and traversal landmarks
tasks.description: Introduce route landmarks and checkpoint progression so movement across the world feels staged, with deliberate transitions from safer spaces into riskier territory.
acceptance: Adventure state tracks checkpoint or landmark ids with discovered/completed state.
The map includes deliberate transition landmarks between early, mid, and late regions rather than only open corridors.
Crossing or activating a checkpoint updates progression state and emits a non-combat progression message.

tasks.title: Model species catalogs and encounter templates
tasks.description: Replace one-off creature definitions with reusable wild-species and enemy-archetype templates tagged by biome and tier so the game can support broader encounter variety.
acceptance: Creature spawn data is expressed through reusable species or archetype templates instead of only inline per-instance stat blocks.
The template catalog covers multiple wild species and multiple enemy archetypes with biome, tier, or weighting metadata.
Creature creation helpers instantiate runtime entities from those templates so later systems can spawn them dynamically.

tasks.title: Add town contracts and staged objective flow
tasks.description: Implement a directed run-goal loop built around town contracts and staged objectives that move the player through checkpoints, encounters, and captures toward a clear late-run target.
acceptance: Adventure state tracks an active contract or objective, its remaining targets, and completed objective history.
Objective logic advances from concrete events such as checkpoint discovery, required defeats, or required captures.
Resolving one contract promotes the next staged goal automatically and ends in a clear late-run objective.

tasks.title: Implement a zone-aware encounter director
tasks.description: Add encounter spawning and repopulation logic that reads biome danger and objective progress so the world stays populated and paced across a longer run.
acceptance: Adventure step logic can spawn or recycle creatures during a run instead of relying only on the initial creature list.
Encounter selection uses zone danger and objective progress so safer routes stay lighter than frontier regions.
Spawn rules protect town space and prevent the world from staying empty after a few fights.

tasks.title: Add distinct enemy behaviors and elite pressure
tasks.description: Make combat less repetitive by introducing differentiated enemy AI profiles and elite variants that change movement, range, attack cadence, and encounter pressure.
acceptance: Enemy archetypes now include more than one combat pattern, such as rushdown, ranged skirmish, or support pressure, instead of sharing one AI loop.
High-tier or elite encounters materially raise pressure through upgraded cadence, range, durability, or support behavior.
Behavior selection is driven by creature or archetype state rather than hardcoding all enemies to the same rules.

tasks.title: Expose capture odds and creature value cues
tasks.description: Deepen capture decisions by surfacing rarity, biome affinity, role, and clearer odds so the player can see why a creature is worth chasing before committing to a catch.
acceptance: Capturable creatures expose value-defining metadata such as rarity, role, biome affinity, or tier in runtime state.
Capture resolution uses that metadata in addition to hp-based weakening so odds or rewards vary meaningfully by target.
The player can read a creature's capture value or odds cue from the adventure HUD or world presentation before attempting a capture.

tasks.title: Add town-side roster management and training
tasks.description: Make captured creatures matter between encounters by adding town interactions for lead-companion selection and coin-backed training or recovery.
acceptance: Adventure state tracks a lead or active companion separately from raw roster order.
Town interaction flow lets the player swap or train companions using existing adventure inputs.
Training or town services spend currency or other adventure resources and persistently update companion stats or readiness.

tasks.title: Make the lead companion affect live gameplay
tasks.description: Ensure roster choices matter during the run by giving the active companion concrete combat or exploration support effects tied to species or role.
acceptance: The selected companion changes live gameplay through a concrete combat or exploration support effect.
Different companion species or roles create different tradeoffs instead of applying one universal bonus.
Adventure step or combat logic reads active-companion data during encounters without requiring changes outside adventure scope.

tasks.title: Upgrade the HUD with objective and zone readability
tasks.description: Improve run-state readability with labeled HUD panels for the current objective, zone danger, checkpoint progress, and lead companion status.
acceptance: The HUD shows current objective or contract progress, current zone or danger tier, and lead companion status.
Primary run stats are presented as labeled panels or readouts instead of only unlabeled bars.
The HUD remains readable on both smaller and larger screens within the existing adventure draw pipeline.

tasks.title: Add milestone banners and event history
tasks.description: Give major progression beats stronger feedback by recording milestones and rendering distinct banners or log entries for checkpoints, contracts, elite wins, and notable captures.
acceptance: Adventure state stores recent milestone or event entries instead of only one transient message string.
Checkpoint clears, contract completions, elite wins, and rare captures each record milestone entries with distinct event types.
Rendering clearly distinguishes major milestone feedback from routine hit, rest, or ambient encounter messages.

tasks.title: Add defeat flow and run summary closure
tasks.description: Create explicit run-end handling and a summary view so longer runs end with clear closure around world progress, captures, and encounter accomplishments.
acceptance: Adventure detects player defeat and final objective completion as explicit run-state transitions.
A summary view or overlay reports concrete run outcomes including discovered zones, completed objectives, captures, and notable fights.
The summary flow preserves enough adventure state to support restart handling or future progression hooks instead of hard-resetting immediately.
